title: Micro review hypotheses and task journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchbook for reviewing small PRs with a measurable hypothesis attached. Not a final checklist — a living journal for experiments + handoffs.

Top-level heuristics (short):
- Make a hypothesis for each sizable change. If patch touches runtime hotpath, hypothesis = measurable perf delta or latency distribution shift.
- Prefer small, verifiable changes: 200–500 LoC max for single risky release.
- Every refactor that renames/reshapes data paths needs a smoke test and a revert path.

Example hypotheses (write before review):
1) "Batching buffer lock moved to shard-level will reduce tail latency variance by >5% for 95th p99 windows on XL models" — measure w/ canary and p95/p99 trace.
2) "Quantization config lives in config v2; switching default to int8 reduces GPU memory per worker by ~12MB without regression on eval prompts" — run eval set and mem profile.

Quick review checklist (fast pass):
- Does the PR state a hypothesis? If no, ask author to add one (short).
- Files changed: skim for new global state, hidden caches, or changes to KV layout.
- Tests: unit, integration, smoke. If none and change touches hotpath, request smoke harness.
- Metrics hooks: is there a metric/tagging hook added? If not, note where to attach.
- Config gating: is change behind feature flag/canary? If not, suggest one for risky changes.
- Rollback: is revert simple? Is there a migration that needs backout?

Deeper pass (if time):
- Read key functions: focus on functions with "hot" comments or marked with // latency-sensitive.
- Grep for calls to global caches: "kv_cache", "shared_pool", "static_cache".
- Grep commands I use: 
  - git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c 'echo --- {}; sed -n "1,200p" {}'
  - rg "kv_cache|shared_pool|atomic|std::mutex|rwlock" -S --hidden
- Microbench plan: add a note to run local tracer on sample workload (sample script: tools/run_trace_local.sh --model=redwood-xl --qps=1 --duration=120)

Risk matrix (quick):
- Low: docs, minor test fixes, non-runtime examples.
- Medium: API shaping, config changes (if behind flag).
- High: runtime path, locking, memory layout, serialization formats.

Action items to leave in PR comments (templated):
- "Add short hypothesis (one line) describing expected user-visible delta."
- "Can we gate this behind a feature flag? If not possible, explain why."
- "Please add a micro-smoke test that reproduces the change surface."
- "Add metric hook at <file>:<line> for measuring (latency/mem/error-rate)."

Follow-up mapping (how I track):
- If I flag a TODO that needs work, create a ticket named "PR462: <short> - follow up" and add crosslink.
- Small fixes can be pushed as post-merge patch if low risk; otherwise block merge.

Notes-to-self:
- Avoid suggesting sweeping renames in review; split into separate PR.
- If author argues no metric needed, require a short note explaining how we'll detect regressions post-merge.
- Keep list of repeated violations: e.g., missing feature flags, no metrics, long-running test flakes — escalate to team retro.

Refactor idea sketch (for later):
- Introduce a small ReviewScore enum for PRs (SHELF, LOW, MED, HIGH) and tag reviews. Use for prioritizing SRE attention.
- Lightweight template generator: "review-hypothesis.md" that auto-fills checklist and grep commands.

Deferred decisions / open questions (for next sync):
- Do we have a standard smoke harness for KV layout changes? If not, propose one (sequence-level tests).
- Can we add an automatic lint that flags missing metric hooks when runtime files are changed?

Quick pro tips (personal):
- Use a single PR browser view and jump to files changed; open two panes if comparing behaviour with main.
- Paste small reproducible steps in PR description — saves cycles.
- If I see a change touching both C++ runtime and python client in same PR, consider splitting.

Recent PR notes (examples to copy):
- "PR#462: moved batch lock; observed p99 tail increase on canary — reverted and opened follow-up ticket RELAY-1283"
- "PR#497: refactor config loader; added flag 'use_new_loader' and smoke tests; metrics added at loader.start"

Checklist for merging risky change (pre-merge):
- [ ] Hypothesis written and measurable metrics identified
- [ ] Canary config exists and is tested for 1% traffic
- [ ] Smoke test passes in staging 3x consecutively
- [ ] Rollback runbook documented in PR description

Random thoughts / brainstorming lines:
- Could we have a "review playground" repo where reviewers can drop changes and run a one-click canary?
- A tiny CI job that builds canary image and runs a standard 10-min workload for p99 checks before merge.

End-of-session TODO (if I close tab):
- Add hypothesis template file to repo: tools/review_hypothesis_template.md
- Open RELAY ticket to capture missing smoke harness for KV changes
- Ping Noelle for metric naming conventions and add to PR template
